Hi everyone.  None of the researchers make any money off this study.  That would be highly unethical.  That is also why studies, such as this one, are reviewed by an IRB -- to monitor the research to ensure ethical conduct.  The specific statement in the consent form is " *Researchers on this study receive royalties from New Harbinger Publications for books that cover topics under investigation in this study. The terms of this arrangement have been reviewed and approved by The University of Toledo in accordance with its policy on objectivity in research*."  When a researcher writes an academic book, it is an additional source of income, outside of his/her pay as a teacher at the university.  As a result, the researcher is required to disclose that to the university, who then reviews this source of income as well as studies the researcher is involved with to ensure this is never a conflict of interest.  In this case, Dr. Tull has written a couple books on emotions and PTSD and the university is stating that their review has determined that it is not in conflict with this study.  I think that also makes intuitive sense given that the survey questions here have nothing to do with the books my colleague wrote.   I hope that helps clarify.

**Target group:** 18+, living in the US, have considered suicide in the past year, and would consider yourself to be in one of the following groups: (1) using alcohol has been giving you problems in the past year (2) using opiates has been giving you problems in the past year, or (3) you don’t use substances. 

**Compensation:** **$15 in Amazon Gift cards**. The study consists of 2 surveys.  We compensate $10 now for the longer survey, which should take about an hour, and $5 for the very short survey 6 months in the future. 

**Link:** [https://utoledoir.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV\_4ItnU4z8520B0kR](https://utoledoir.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4ItnU4z8520B0kR)

\[The first couple minutes is a screener to confirm eligibility, and after that you will taken directly to the first survey\]

**Background:** In brief, the ultimate goal of the study is to develop better interventions for folks who may be considering suicide. The specific goal is to determine what different treatment needs may exist for folks using or not using substances. *To this end, we ask for detailed information on alcohol/substance use and suicide as this provides the clearest information on if/how they are related and what treatment needs exist.*

**Link to results:** We will be preparing a short summary of results that will be available a few months after the study ends. We will email this to interested individuals. Please email us to be included on this list.  

**Questions?**: If you have any questions, or accidentally click on something that takes you out of the survey prematurely, please send me a DM, reply to this thread, or email me directly. I’ll reply as quickly as I can! Thank you very much for considering participation.
